samples.question: Thin gray lines split this image into four square panels side by side, counted from the left. Each panel contains one ring drawn as a circle outline with a single opening cut out of it, and one small filled dot lying outside that ring. A dot faces its ring's opening when the straight direction from the centre of that ring to that dot passes through the opening rather than through the drawn part of the ring. Exactly one panel has its dot facing its own opening; in every other panel the direction to the dot misses the opening by more than fourteen degrees. Every ring has the same radius, and opening width, dot distance, dot colour, ring colour, panel position and the amount of ink in a panel carry no information about the answer: the facing panel is not systematically the one with the widest or the narrowest opening, nor the one with the nearest or the farthest dot. Compare each dot only with the ring in its own panel. Which half of the image contains the panel whose dot faces its ring's opening, given that the first two panels form the left half and the last two form the right half? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.
